subject.title: Crestodian chat hijacks natural language into operations; approvals require a literal hardcoded yes

question: Should Crestodian normal chat become strictly AI-first, with deterministic parsing limited to exact typed commands and rescue/no-model fallback while preserving explicit approval boundaries for setup and plugin-installing flows?
rationale: The source supports real bugs, but the repair changes setup UX, approval intent, rescue behavior, agent-loop directives, and security boundaries, so maintainer intent should define the durable contract before merge.

options.title: Adopt AI-first boundary
options.body: Route normal natural-language chat through the model, keep deterministic grammar exact and fallback-only, and fix approval, stale-proposal, redaction, and Gemini parity together.

options.title: Ship parser safety first
options.body: Anchor the riskiest deterministic command parsing and broaden host approval handling while leaving directives and executor refactor work for follow-up.

options.title: Split the umbrella
options.body: Keep this as canonical but require separate smaller PRs for parser safety, approval intent, stale proposal handling, secret-history redaction, executor structure, and Gemini parity.

recommendation.title: Adopt AI-first boundary
recommendation.body: Route normal natural-language chat through the model, keep deterministic grammar exact and fallback-only, and fix approval, stale-proposal, redaction, and Gemini parity together.

likelyOwner.reason: The central Crestodian feature history and current issue/PR ownership point to steipete as the best product-boundary owner.
